The Sibylvariant Transform (Sibylvariant Transform) is a new technique for synthetic data generation within Natural Language Processing (NLP). It is designed to create diverse language variations that preserve the original semantic meaning of the source text. By enabling the robustness of machine learning models through enhanced data augmentation, this approach helps them better handle real-world language variability. Research findings indicate that the Sibylvariant transformation is more effective than existing state-of-the-art augmentation methods for classifying text, specifically demonstrating superior performance on tasks such as hate speech and abusive content detection.

This work presents the first rigorous theoretical framework for meta-learning a linear representation that enables robust generalization to novel tasks. Our approach adapts to tasks characterized by intrinsic dimensionality $d^*$ within an ambient space of dimension $d$, where $d^*$ is significantly smaller than $d$. We demonstrate the existence of an efficient gradient descent-based meta-learning algorithm capable of learning this representation from $d$-dimensional data, with sample complexity scaling as $O(d^* \cdot \text{polylog}(d))$. Furthermore, we establish that our method offers strong robustness against intrinsic dimension shifts when encountering new tasks.

Neural machine translation (NMT) models are typically large, memory-intensive, and difficult to deploy on devices with limited resources. To address this, several methods have been developed to compress these models, including knowledge distillation and quantization. However, the impact of these techniques on model stability and output quality remains unclear. This study evaluates various combinations of distillation and quantization to create efficient, resource-constrained multilingual translation models. Our findings indicate that while quantization and KDDistill shrink model parameters, quantization is more effective at reducing model size and improving translation quality than KDDistillation. Additionally, the research reveals that these techniques can make NMTs brittle, causing performance to degrade significantly under low hyperparameter settings. Finally, this study suggests that mixed precision training is a viable alternative approach for compressing multilingual models.

Deep learning models typically demand vast amounts of labeled data to achieve high performance, a challenge that is particularly acute in medical imaging, where expert annotation is time-consuming and labor-intensive. This study addresses the scarcity of labeled data in lung imaging by investigating how image augmentation techniques impact the training of segmentation models for detecting pneumonia in chest X-rays. Utilizing the Pneumonia Chest X-ray dataset from Kaggle, we evaluated several augmentation strategies to determine their effect on model accuracy. Our findings indicate that applying these augmentations significantly lowered the requirement for labeled data without compromising performance. Specifically, we demonstrated that a model trained with a 20% label rate on augmented data outperformed one trained on the full dataset of un-augented images. Furthermore, this approach exhibited strong generalization capabilities across different patient demographics.

Image captioning is a natural language generation task that involves describing an image using a single paragraph. While recent advancements in image captioning have produced impressive results, they typically rely on a fixed template that hinders the ability to customize captions according to specific user requirements. To address this gap, we introduce a new framework called Image Captioning with Prompt Control (ICPC), which utilizes prompt engineering to generate image descriptions that align with user-specified constraints. By leveraging the underlying capabilities of large language models, our approach offers flexible, controllable image captioning. We demonstrate that a model trained on standard datasets can be effectively adapted to meet specific criteria without any additional training data. Furthermore, we identify a previously overlooked challenge in the field: controllable image captioning under multiple constraints. Extensive experiments across various scenarios confirm that our proposed method is both simple and highly effective.

This paper introduces a novel framework for modeling the causal effects of actions, which also provides a new definition for defining intentional harms within the framework. In contrast with the traditional definition, our approach handles cases where the agent does not intend the specific outcome that eventually occurs. We formalize our approach using STRIPS planning and demonstrate that, in contrast with the traditional approach, our method can identify intentional harms in a wider range of scenarios. We also discuss the advantages and limitations of our approach.

This study introduces an open-source library named MMLSpark, which is built to facilitate the deployment of deep learning models within Apache Spark ecosystems. Our objective is to create an open and adaptable interface that streamlines the development of scalable deep learning algorithms. MMLSpark supports various neural network architectures, including Feed Forward Neural Networks (NNs), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs). Furthermore, it offers built-in support for training on massive datasets by utilizing distributed computing resources. Our findings indicate that MMLSpark successfully delivers a user-friendly method for constructing and training neural networks at scale, while maintaining high flexibility and adaptability across different data types and workloads.

Speech translation involves converting spoken language from one source into another. This research explores the feasibility of implementing "zero-shot" translation using deep learning models trained exclusively on unlabeled audio data, without any parallel labeled pairs for training translation. We introduce a framework that leverages unsupervised speech clustering to generate synthetic pseudo-parallel data for automatic model pre-training. We examine this problem through the task of zero-shot translation and demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art systems that utilize large, annotated speech-to-speech translation datasets.

Accurate short-term energy demand prediction is critical for the operational management of electricity grids, particularly as the transition to decentralized generation and the integration of distributed energy resources reshape the traditional power balance. This paper presents a probabilistic load forecasting model specifically designed for distribution transformers, utilizing smart meter data. The proposed approach combines a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network with Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling to generate probabilistic forecasts that account for various sources of uncertainty. Furthermore, the study evaluates a fusion strategy that merges household-level consumption forecasts to produce estimates at the transformer level. The accuracy of these probabilistic forecasts is benchmarked against the performance of the fused load estimates relative to actual aggregated data.

This paper introduces a comprehensive framework for integrating machine learning (ML) with domain-specific knowledge. While contemporary ML methods have demonstrated remarkable efficacy in numerous applications, their "black-box" nature often creates conflicts with regulatory mandates and ethical standards that necessitate interpretability. We propose a structured taxonomy to guide the systematic incorporation of domain knowledge into the ML development lifecycle. Specifically, our framework categorizes this knowledge by its granularity and functional role within model training, validation, and deployment. We further outline strategic pathways to achieve interpretability and highlight strategic synergies between various framework components. Finally, we illustrate the practical utility of this approach through a detailed case study in medical image analysis.

The ongoing COVID-19 pandemic has spurred significant research into the early detection of the disease through lung lesion analysis on chest CT scans. Existing supervised learning methods for localizing and segmenting these lesions face challenges due to the scarcity of large-scale datasets and the prohibitive cost of manual annotation. This work introduces a novel, cost-effective approach to generate high-quality training data using weak supervision, based on a new framework combining deep learning and a pre-trained model. This method enables accurate lesion segmentation without necessitating detailed pixel-level labels. We evaluated the system on the widely recognized COVID-CT-14 dataset, comparing it against established baseline techniques. The results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves superior performance in both sensitivity and specificity compared to the benchmarks.

Accurate localization and identification of vertebrae are critical for various clinical tasks, including spine disease detection, treatment planning, and surgical navigation. However, these tasks remain difficult due to significant variations in vertebral anatomy, the presence of artifacts, and the lack of distinctive features between adjacent vertebrae. This study introduces a novel method for localization and identification that integrates end-to-end training, anatomical constraints, and optimization strategies. The approach utilizes a U-Net architecture to generate initial localization and identification results, which are subsequently refined through a vertebrae rectification module. This module aligns the raw CT slices with the axial plane and standardizes inter-vertebral spacing, thereby enhancing model performance. Additionally, an identification refinement stage employs anatomical constraints and an optimization framework to correct potential errors from the initial prediction. The proposed method was evaluated on the ISIC 2018 Spine CT dataset, achieving a mean localization error of 1.76 vertebrae and a mean identification error of 0.88 vertebrae.

We introduce a novel mechanism for dynamical stabilization, wherein a moving particle within a cavity experiences resilience against ionization or decay due to fluctuations in the cavity vacuum. This phenomenon is examined in the context of resonant electron elastic scattering involving a bound state attached to one of the scattering particles, operating within the strong light-matter regime. Our analysis demonstrates that, under specific conditions, the interaction between the scattering process and light-matter coupling can drastically alter the scattering matrix. Notably, this effect can be observed even when the dynamical states of the system are treated as classical entities.

This paper presents a method for enhancing quadruped locomotion by training elastic actuators to exploit their passive properties. We introduce a new loss function grounded in the principle of actuator exploitation, which directs elastic actuators to perform work that facilitates locomotion. Our approach employs a two-stage training framework: first, a static stage optimizes velocities separately for walking and galloping patterns, followed by a dynamic stage where joint torques are computed based on a forward kinematic model. Evaluating this method on the OpenLAMB platform demonstrates that learned exploited elastic actuators achieve superior locomotion efficiency and stability when integrated with existing control strategies.

This study examines the evolution of a small-scale tearing mode in a collisionless slab plasma, specifically investigating the mode's development from an initial linear phase to its nonlinear saturation state. Central to this investigation is the identification of the mechanisms governing magnetic reconnection and the transport of particles and energy during the saturation phase. Utilizing the two-dimensional, electrostatically screened, collisionless, drift-reduced hybrid-Vlasov model, the research focuses on electron kinetics to analyze these phenomena. The findings indicate that, during linear growth, the instability is driven by the mirror mode, which arises from the mirror instability present in the electron velocity distribution function. In the nonlinear regime, the island coalescence mechanism is responsible for saturating the mode's growth. Furthermore, the study reveals that reconnection in this collisionless environment is primarily controlled by the transport processes occurring at the island separatrix, an area characterized by significant mirror-trapped particle populations.

We present a novel approach to attribute manipulation fashion image retrieval, which focuses on altering specific features within a single image to generate a new visual instance. This method introduces a semi-supervised learning framework designed to enhance performance under scarce labeled data conditions by leveraging unlabeled samples to refine model accuracy. Additionally, we introduce a new dataset tailored to evaluate feature-level attribute manipulation retrieval. Finally, we provide comprehensive results that demonstrate the efficacy of this semi-supervised learning system.

This work introduces a novel dual gradient flow designed to address linear ill-posed equations within the framework of Banach spaces. We demonstrate that the flow generates a conditional stable algorithm when a specific stopping criterion is applied. Furthermore, the approach is broadened to the domain of linear multi-parameter ill-posed problems, establishing a dual interpretation for a recently developed multi-parameter dual regularization method originally formulated by the authors in [2018,2020].

We introduce a cost construction technique for light field depth estimation that explicitly models occlusions. By treating the construction of pixel-level cost volumes as a regression task, the method predicts both a per-pixel reference depth map and the variance of that depth to create a pixel-level transparency mask. This mask is then integrated into the cost volume generation process, yielding a refined estimation of pixel occlusions. Ultimately, the enhanced depth map accurately identifies occluded regions, significantly boosting performance in visual tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior quality compared to previous methods in light field 3D reconstruction applications.

Non-Riemannian gravity theories have recently garnered significant interest due to their potential advantages over standard Einstein-Hilbert gravity in specific cosmological scenarios. Within double field theory (DBT), a unified framework that treats space and time on equal footing, we derive action functionals for various such gravities. By imposing the DFT strong section condition at the level of the equations of motion, we establish consistent gravitational models that are distinctly non-Riemannian.

The proliferation of IoT devices and the widespread adoption of high-bandwidth applications, such as video streaming, have intensified the demand for wireless networks capable of delivering superior Quality of Service (QoS). In this context, the study examines the performance of home WiFi networks equipped with multiple Access Points (APs) and network extenders. Building on this, the research introduces a client association algorithm that leverages IEEE 802.11k and v standards to assess channel load across all available home APs and extenders. By incorporating channel load awareness, the proposed scheme enhances network throughput and user experience. Furthermore, the study explores the role of network extenders in facilitating channel load balancing and increasing user throughput within multi-AP environments.
